key_insight: PI-GINOT learns geometry-dependent finite-strain hyperelastic responses for parametric DogBone specimens without using finite-element training data.
engineering_relevance: It offers a data-free surrogate for virtual testing and design studies when geometry changes make repeated nonlinear solid-mechanics simulations expensive.
method: Encodes each specimen from a boundary point cloud into geometry features.
Uses a cross-attention decoder to predict displacement at arbitrary points.
Enforces boundary conditions exactly and trains with physics losses from equilibrium, traction-free/symmetry conditions, stability, and internal force consistency.
evidence_signal: Validated on eight unseen geometries with Abaqus, the model reports 2.1%–7.1% displacement error, 0.9%–13.3% peak von Mises stress error, and section-force error below 10.3%.
watch_item: Local stress components can still be inaccurate near steep gradients, especially for narrow specimens around the gauge-to-fillet transition.
paper_title: PI-GINOT: Data-free geometry-informed neural operator learning for finite-strain hyperelasticity on parametric DogBone specimens
